rows.uncertainty: Very short report (2 pages, 'Therapeutic challenge' format) with no patient or lesion count, no skin type, no body site, no assessment method and no follow-up interval. Internal conflict: the text says 2 sittings 1 month apart yielded complete uniform repigmentation (Fig 1, A and B), but the Fig 1 caption says the follow-up photo is 'after (B) a single needling sitting'; whether the result followed one or two sittings is unclear. Time from the final treatment to the follow-up photo is not reported, so months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE; the claim that 5-FU 'makes a long-lasting favorable microenvironment' is not supported by any follow-up data in the report. Authors state 'This is an off-label use of 5-fluorouracil and the safety and efficacy remain unknown.' The outcome is a qualitative claim, not a measured endpoint, so the tier is unquantified. IRB approval 'Not applicable'.
rows.citation: Rambhia SH, Rambhia KD. Treatment of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis with 5-fluorouracil tattooing using a handheld needle. JAAD Int 2020;1(2):200-201

A simple 24-gauge hypodermic needle was dipped in a vial containing a solution of 5-fluorouracil at 50 mg/mL.
the tip of the needle was later inserted in the lesion to create mild pinpoint bleeding under aseptic conditions.
We conducted a total of 2 sittings 1 month apart
